title: Spectral Optimization for Absolutely PPT States: Purity, Entropy, and Volume Decay
abstract: We study maximum purity and minimum von Neumann entropy of absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) states, together with the relative volume of their spectral sets. A consequence of Hildebrand's criterion gives an explicit outer spectral polytope, whose vertices we classify. Optimizing purity over this polytope, together with the Song--Chen result for the $2\otimes3$ system, yields, for every $mn\ge6$, an explicit upper bound on the purity of APPT states that is asymptotic to $4/(3mn)$. This improves the previous $2/(mn)$ upper bound for absolutely separable states. The new bound applies to every APPT state, a class containing all absolutely separable states, and is sharp for every $2\otimes n$ system with $n\ge3$. For every $3\otimes n$ system with $n\ge3$, however, the unique outer-polytope maximizer is not APPT, so the bound is strict and disproves the Dũng--Khôi qutrit--qudit conjecture. The polytope also gives an explicit entropy lower bound in arbitrary bipartite dimensions and, together with the Song--Chen extreme-point classification, the exact minimum entropy for every $2\otimes n$ system. Finally, exact formulas for the relative volumes of an inner polytope and the outer spectral polytope give explicit two-sided bounds on the qubit--qudit relative spectral volume $a_n$ whose ratio is less than $4$ and tends to $3$. Consequently, $a_n=Θ\!\left(\sqrt n(4/27)^n\right)$, and the relative volume of the qubit--qudit APPT spectral set (equivalently, the absolutely separable spectral set) has exact exponential decay rate $\ln(27/4)$.
summary: This paper provides a deep mathematical analysis of spectral properties for Absolutely PPT quantum states in bipartite systems. It derives sharp upper bounds for purity and determines the minimum entropy for specific dimensions. Crucially, it quantifies the exponential decay rate of the spectral volume, offering precise tools for characterizing quantum state sets.
main_problem: The paper investigates the maximum purity, minimum von Neumann entropy, and relative spectral volume of Absolutely PPT (APPT) quantum states.
main_result: It establishes a dimension-dependent upper bound on the purity of APPT states, improves previous bounds, and determines the exact exponential decay rate of the spectral volume for qubit-qudit systems.
method: The research combines optimization techniques over explicitly defined outer spectral polytopes with rigorous mathematical analysis, including interval arithmetic for entropy bounding.
model_or_system: The study focuses on bipartite quantum states $ho$ on $C^m \otimes C^n$, specifically analyzing the properties of APPT states, which are constrained by linear matrix inequalities derived from the PPT condition.
key_observables: Purity ($	ext{Tr}(ho^2)$), Von Neumann Entropy ($S(ho)$), and the relative spectral volume of the state set ($	ext{rvol}(\Lambda_{	ext{APPT}})$).
important_parameters: Bipartite dimensions ($m, n$), and the asymptotic ratio of volumes, which tends to 3.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on characterizing the APPT property via the outer spectral polytope and assumes that optimization over this polytope yields the extremal values.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing purity bounds and disproving conjectures for specific dimensions ($3\otimes n$). It then tackles the minimum entropy for $2\otimes n$ systems, followed by detailed calculations of the relative spectral volume decay rate, and finally, rigorous bounding of the entropy minimum using interval arithmetic.
why_interesting: The work provides sharp, quantitative bounds on fundamental quantum information measures (purity, entropy) for a physically relevant class of states (APPT), which has implications for understanding entanglement and separability in multipartite systems.
